original_failure.evidence_boundary: Independently read and hash-checked the complete original log. It records an empty PID parse at the ready reader. The exact scheduling interleaving and seed were not captured, so no new syscall trace/reproduction is claimed. The identical vulnerable source blob is present at fixedPR180.

diagnosis: The old helper created final ready before write_all and sync_all. Parent exists() could therefore succeed before PID bytes existed. The old parent immediately read and parsed the empty file, matching the observed panic. This is a fixture publication race; oldfailed execution remains failed.
change_and_justification: Only signal_and_wait changes: durable writesPID to ready.pending; durable's existing write_all/sync_all complete and its File drops on return; rename then publishes ready in the same fresh per-case directory.

Both names share a directory/filesystem. Parent watches only ready, so it cannot read the pending inode during creation/writing. Atomic name publication exposes completePID bytes before the unchanged parent read/parse.

The owner already refuses reused per-case directories with create_dir. One ownedchild reaches signal_and_wait once and parks. The new pending name is not a second writer, a retry or a reused successful marker.

Write/sync/rename errors retain unwrap propagation. Child failure is still observed by the original try_wait/deadline loop; malformed/wrongPID stays a strict parse/equality failure. No empty-PID retry or error swallowing is added.
This preserves the existing process-crash test scope; it does not introduce a power-loss durability guarantee or alter production cache/database writes.
